major_resolutions: Hengyang airfield/outer node is reached and physically denied/captured by early June, but Hengyang city remains Chinese and becomes a methodical siege/reduction problem.
China progression is recorded as layered transfer of rail/river/air/admin functions, not map color alone.
US June fast-carrier OOB is rebuilt to 8 CV + 8 CVL in the Branch before FORAGER combat.
I-400/I-401 six-Seiran system passes readiness and spends its first-strike surprise against Majuro logistics on 3 Jun.
Majuro strike creates real ammunition/service friction and slight sortie staggering but does not cancel FORAGER or move the 15 Jun D-Day.
Yamamoto retains the five-carrier main force for amphibious-triggered counterstroke rather than reacting to the logistics raid result.
75mm turreted stopgap receives low-rate pilot-series authorization; no combat fielding yet.
forward_constraints: Do not mark Hengyang city captured before a new siege/assault adjudication.

Do not restore historical 7-CV/8-CVL TF58 count.
Do not give the Seiran raid a strategic kill beyond the specified logistics friction.
